hero.title: AI system
hero.lead: My first agent pipeline: it takes a task from plan to code to pull request, and learns from its own runs.

sections.title: Where it's at
paragraphs: My first agent pipeline ran from May to September 2026. It took real tasks from a ticket to a pull request, on its own code and on Duo Decide. I'm now building the next version, Distill, with a coworker, and this pipeline is being retired as Distill takes over.

stops.title: Lessons
stops.text: Repeated failures become ranked lessons the planner can pull, behind a gate built to say no.

expanders.title: What I'm building
paragraphs: One system that runs the whole loop (plan, build, check, open a pull request) and gets better from its own history. The rule of the house: the model picks what; code picks where and how.

expanders.title: What I tried
paragraphs: A panel of twelve critic personas debating each plan. An evidence stage that reproduces the problem before any planning. A ledger that records every run, and a weekly job that ranks repeated failures into lessons. A board with its own design system, so agents building UI could read the mocks. Spend caps per run and per stage from the first day.

artifacts.title: Spend caps
artifacts.text: Three Duo Decide runs stopped at the code stage when they reached their spend cap, and waited there to resume.

image.alt: The board dashboard with three Duo Decide runs paused at the code stage after reaching their budget. Spend figures are masked.

artifacts.title: First proof
artifacts.text: Five runs on two repos finished with no interventions, and the first two lessons came out of them.

artifacts.title: Data first
artifacts.text: An inventory found lots of code, zero real runs and an empty ledger. I stopped adding features and fed it real tickets.

expanders.title: What didn't work
paragraphs: The lesson loop was wired but starved. When I audited it in July, 60 of 73 runs had pulled in no lessons at all. The gate was doing its job: every lesson was about how runs fail, so it rightly said no to product work. The weekly job that made lessons had also run once and never again, because it was scheduled for an hour when my machine was asleep. Real improvement was coming from the pipeline's own review loop, not from the lessons.

artifacts.title: The lesson loop starved
artifacts.text: 60 of 73 runs pulled in no lessons. The weekly job had run once, at an hour my machine was asleep.

image.alt: The board's Memory view: a table of runs with status, repo, tokens and whether each run produced memory. Spend is masked.

artifacts.title: The doc was wrong
text: The pipeline followed Duo Decide's voting doc to the letter, and vote decisions stuck for three months.

artifacts.text: The board was made for a desk. On a phone, the sidebar fills the top half of the screen.

expanders.title: Open questions and next
paragraphs: What carries forward to the next version is the habit: run real work first, record every run, and measure before trusting a stage. Still open: a cheaper model first, with a verifier deciding when to escalate, and better memory search for questions worded differently from the lesson.

artifacts.title: The top lesson
artifacts.text: Repeated retries at the code stage: seen 23 times across 3 repos. One of 14 lessons the ledger produced.
